Tomato Early Blight.recommendation: Prune and dispose of infected lower leaves immediately. Apply copper-based or chlorothalonil fungicide every 7-10 days during warm, humid conditions.
preventative_measures: Water at the base of the plant to keep foliage dry (use drip irrigation)
Maintain a 2-3 year crop rotation away from nightshade family crops
Mulch soil around plants to prevent fungal spores from splashing onto leaves
Ensure proper plant spacing for adequate air circulation
Tomato Early Blight.organic_options: Apply organic copper spray or Bacillus subtilis bio-fungicide weekly.

Tomato Late Blight.recommendation: Remove and destroy all heavily infected plants immediately to prevent rapid airborne spread. Treat surrounding healthy plants with preventive mancozeb or copper fungicide.
preventative_measures: Plant certified disease-resistant tomato varieties
Avoid overhead watering, especially late in the afternoon
Destroy volunteer tomato and potato plants near the field
Monitor weather forecasts for cool, wet conditions favorable to blight
Tomato Late Blight.organic_options: Copper hydroxide formulations applied strictly as preventative measures before rains.

Tomato Healthy.recommendation: No disease detected. Continue standard agronomic practices, balanced fertilization, and routine pest scouting.
preventative_measures: Maintain consistent soil moisture and avoid waterlogged roots
Apply balanced NPK fertilizer with calcium to avoid blossom end rot
Scout lower leaves weekly for early signs of fungal or bacterial spotting
Sanitize pruning shears between plants
Tomato Healthy.organic_options: Use compost tea or seaweed extract foliar spray for natural plant vigor.

Potato Early Blight.recommendation: Apply protectant fungicides such as chlorothalonil or azoxystrobin. Ensure nitrogen fertilization is balanced to prevent premature vine senescence.
preventative_measures: Use certified disease-free seed tubers
Rotate with non-solanaceous crops like corn, beans, or grains
Avoid sprinkler irrigation during late afternoon or overcast days
Hill up soil well to protect developing tubers from spore wash
Potato Early Blight.organic_options: Copper soap fungicide and potassium bicarbonate sprays.

Potato Late Blight.recommendation: Act urgently: cut and destroy vines if harvest is near to prevent tuber infection, or apply systemic fungicides (e.g., cymoxanil or mandipropamid) immediately.
preventative_measures: Eliminate cull piles and volunteer potatoes in the surrounding vicinity
Allow at least 2 weeks between vine killing and harvest for skin set
Store tubers in well-ventilated, cool storage areas
Inspect foliage every 3 to 4 days during humid, overcast periods
Potato Late Blight.organic_options: Bordeaux mixture (copper sulfate + lime) applied early in the growth season.

Potato Healthy.recommendation: No disease detected. Potato canopy is vigorous. Ensure steady moisture during tuber initiation and bulk growth.
preventative_measures: Hill soil around plant base to prevent tuber greening and pest access
Maintain proper spacing to optimize sunlight penetration and air movement
Avoid excess nitrogen application after tuber initiation
Inspect underside of foliage weekly for pest or blight symptoms
Potato Healthy.organic_options: Apply kelp meal and bio-stimulants to strengthen tuber development.

Pepper Bacterial Spot.recommendation: Apply fixed copper bactericide combined with mancozeb for improved bacterial control. Avoid working in the field when plants are wet.
preventative_measures: Use hot-water treated or certified disease-free seeds and transplants
Sanitize stakes, trays, and gardening tools with 10% bleach solution
Practice minimum 1-year rotation away from peppers and tomatoes
Avoid overhead sprinkler irrigation
Pepper Bacterial Spot.organic_options: Copper octanoate (copper soap) spray combined with neem oil extract.

Pepper Healthy.recommendation: No disease detected. Foliage is healthy. Maintain consistent irrigation and balanced nutrition for blossom and fruit development.
preventative_measures: Provide consistent drip irrigation to avoid blossom end drop
Mulch beds to regulate soil temperature and conserve moisture
Maintain soil pH between 6.0 and 6.8 for optimal nutrient uptake
Monitor for aphids and whiteflies that can vector viral diseases
Pepper Healthy.organic_options: Foliar spray with fish emulsion and compost tea during active vegetative growth.

Corn Common Rust.recommendation: Foliar fungicides (such as strobilurin or triazole classes) are effective if applied at the first sign of pustules prior to tasseling.
preventative_measures: Plant rust-resistant hybrid corn cultivars
Plant early in the season to avoid late-season spore influxes
Maintain balanced soil fertility and avoid excessive nitrogen
Destroy or till under crop residues after harvest
Corn Common Rust.organic_options: Sulfur dusts or bio-fungicide sprays applied at first sign of rust pustules.

Apple Apple Scab.recommendation: Rake and compost or burn fallen leaves in autumn to eliminate overwintering spores. Apply captan or myclobutanil fungicide starting at green tip stage.
preventative_measures: Prune apple trees during dormancy to open canopy for rapid leaf drying
Select scab-resistant apple cultivars (e.g., Liberty, Freedom, Enterprise)
Apply urea spray to fallen leaves to accelerate leaf breakdown
Avoid overhead watering on the orchard canopy
Apple Apple Scab.organic_options: Lime sulfur or liquid copper sprays applied during dormant and green tip bud stages.
